migration_steps.activity: Emergency containment and forensic validation of compromised RSA-1024 certificate scope; inventory all TLS endpoints, certificate stores, and dependent services.
prerequisites: Access to certificate inventory and CMDB

migration_steps.activity: Immediate replacement of compromised RSA-1024 certificates with RSA-2048/3072 or ECDSA P-256 certificates as an interim secure baseline; revoke all RSA-1024 certificates.
prerequisites: Certificate authority (CA) able to issue RSA-2048/3072 or ECDSA P-256 certificates

migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration governance: CISO steering committee, cryptographic inventory, risk register, and formal rejection of non-standard vendor algorithm pending independent review.
Conduct independent technical and security review of the vendor's non-NIST 'quantum-safe' solution; require third-party cryptanalysis, FIPS 140-3 validation status, and interoperability evidence.
prerequisites: Vendor submits algorithm specification and security proofs

migration_steps.activity: Define target PQC architecture using NIST-standardized algorithms: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key establishment and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for digital signatures; map to TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange and certificate authentication.
Assess vendor and platform PQC readiness: TLS terminators, load balancers, HSMs, CAs, operating systems, and application libraries; document confirmed vs claimed capabilities.
Build and test PQC hybrid TLS (ML-KEM + classical) and ML-DSA certificate authentication in non-production lab; validate performance, interoperability, and fallback behavior.
prerequisites: Step 6 vendor readiness confirmed for at least one platform
HSM firmware supporting ML-KEM/ML-DSA available (or software fallback approved)
Test certificates issued by PQC-capable CA

migration_steps.activity: Pilot PQC hybrid TLS on low-risk external-facing services with monitoring and rollback plan; collect operational metrics.
Phased production rollout of PQC hybrid TLS and ML-DSA certificates across remaining systems, prioritized by risk and vendor support availability.
prerequisites: Vendor production support confirmed for each platform
Change freezes respected (no rollout during quarter-end freezes)

migration_steps.activity: Decommission legacy RSA-1024 and non-standard algorithms; update cryptographic policy and continuous monitoring.
prerequisites: All systems validated against PQC policy

blockers.blocker: Vendor solution is not NIST-standardized and claims to be 'better than NIST'.
blockers.reason: Non-standard cryptography lacks public cryptanalysis, interoperability, and regulatory acceptance; using it could create new vulnerabilities and compliance failures.
blockers.resolution_required: Independent third-party cryptanalysis, published security proofs, FIPS 140-3 validation evidence, and interoperability test results. If not provided, reject vendor solution and use NIST FIPS 203/204.

blockers.blocker: CISO's 3-month timeline for full PQC migration is not achievable.
blockers.reason: PQC standards, vendor support, HSM firmware, CA capabilities, and testing cycles require 12-18 months for a financial services firm; 3 months is insufficient for safe production migration.
blockers.resolution_required: Executive re-baselining of timeline with phased milestones; immediate interim remediation (RSA-2048/ECDSA) within 3 months, full PQC in 12-18 months.

blockers.blocker: Only $700,000 remains after $300,000 incident response commitment.
blockers.reason: Full PQC migration including HSMs, CA upgrades, vendor licensing, testing, and staff training typically exceeds $700,000.
blockers.resolution_required: Prioritize spend on interim certificate replacement and lab validation; seek additional budget or phase migration across fiscal years.

blockers.blocker: PQC support in TLS terminators, HSMs, and CAs is not confirmed.
blockers.reason: Many vendors have announced but not shipped ML-KEM/ML-DSA support; production deployment cannot proceed without validated firmware and certificates.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written vendor roadmaps with committed dates, firmware versions, and validation evidence; do not schedule production changes before confirmation.

blockers.blocker: Financial services regulatory approval for PQC algorithms and certificate authorities may be required.
blockers.reason: Regulators may require notification or approval before changing cryptographic controls; non-standard algorithms likely prohibited.
blockers.resolution_required: Engage compliance and regulators early; document use of NIST-standardized algorithms only.

blockers.blocker: Change freezes and downtime limits restrict production changes.
blockers.reason: Quarter-end and month-end freezes in financial services limit windows for certificate replacement and PQC rollout.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule changes outside freeze periods; obtain emergency change approval for compromised certificate replacement.

vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Independent cryptanalysis, FIPS 140-3 validation, interoperability test reports, published algorithm specification, and security proofs
Written confirmation of ML-KEM and ML-DSA support, firmware version, release date, and test results
FIPS 140-3 validation for ML-KEM/ML-DSA, firmware version, and performance benchmarks
Confirmation of ML-DSA certificate issuance, CRL/OCSP support, and root program acceptance
Support statements for OpenSSL 3.5+ or equivalent, ML-KEM/ML-DSA integration, and patch availability

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment (FIPS 203) for TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange; replaces RSA/ECDH key transport and key agreement.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures (FIPS 204) for certificate authentication and code signing; replaces RSA/ECDSA signatures.

cost_assumptions.category: Independent cryptographic review of vendor solution
CA and certificate lifecycle tooling upgrade

raw_response.confidence: Medium-low: immediate certificate replacement is achievable within 3 months, but full PQC migration depends on unconfirmed vendor support, regulatory approval, and budget constraints; non-standard vendor solution is high risk and should be rejected pending evidence.
